newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil tax cuts linked by cenbank to rate spread.
newsitem.headline: Brazil tax cuts linked by cenbank to rate spread.

text.p: Brazilian Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola on Friday said reductions in a host of taxes for foreign investors were prompted by a narrowing in the spread between domestic and international interest rates.
"The lower the difference between domestic and international interest rates, the less need there is for the IOF (financial transaction taxes)," Loyola told reporters at a news conference.
Brazilian interest rates have fallen by four basis points a month since October and are expected to average about 12 percent annually this year from about 17 percent last year.
But the Central Bank halted its rate decline this month, deciding to leave May rates unchanged from April, fearing rates were falling too far to continue to attract short-term flows.
Still, Loyola suggested cutting the IOF tax made it possible for the government to continue with its policy of interest rate cuts.
"This is no sign of any reversion of our long-term policy, which is a reduction of interest rates. I think Brazil's interest rates are still high," Loyola said.
Returning to the tax cuts themselves, Loyola said they were not designed to stimulate or discourage capital flows but to keep reserves at their current level of about $58 billion.
"We are not trying to stimulate capital flows. What we are trying to do is not discourage them," he said.
He said the tax cuts were precautionary measures aimed at avoiding a bigger problem down the road.
"When you're on a plane, you don't want to see the pilot praying nor sleeping," Loyola said.
He also reiterated the government's belief that the economy was not expanding fast enough overall to warrant measures to slow growth.
